case.summary: Case HHG-004 (card C08106-K1) is verdict uncertain at p=0.58 on customer C08106's denial of a $128.33 online purchase (txn 3583227, product code C, hotmail.com recipient), the sole episode member and full exposure. Candidate pattern is card_not_present_new_device: the transaction ran on a device profile (NULL | NULL | firefox 47.0 | NULL) used for the first time ever on this card, in a two-transaction 48h chain, but the profile is not strong and shows no ring, card-testing, or burst signature. The decisive evidence is mixed across families: the customer-family denial sets the R2/R7 floor at 0.55, and case-memory shows three prior confirmed_fraud closures on this same card (CC-3778, CC-2121, CC-1736, all card_not_present_fraud) pushing toward fraud, while the case-memory calibration score is very low (cms_p 0.00701) and recurring_charge_check/card_testing_check/shared_origin_scan all came back empty, pulling toward legitimate — a genuine single-signal conflict that kept probability in the 0.55-0.70 band. A step-up authentication was requested per R1/§3b; the reply was assumed inconclusive (not completed within the window). The recommended route is auto/L1: CREATE_CASE and MONITOR_CARD remain in force, and DECLINE_TRANSACTION (L1) applies to any pending authorization under R4 pending the customer's reply; the alternative reading — that this is simply an unremembered charge on the customer's own recurring hotmail.com pattern (as with the cleared CC-0696 travel case) — cannot be ruled out and would flip the verdict to legitimate if the step-up succeeds.
